lessons.title: Cameroon: location, relief, climate, rivers and vegetation
lessons.programRef: GCE O Level Geography — Regional geography: Cameroon (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Locate Cameroon and name its neighbours and regions
Describe the climates, rivers and vegetation of Cameroon in their regional pattern
reviewNotes: Facts to verify: the area (about 475 000 km²), the ten regions, plateau altitudes (about 650 m and 1 000 m), the Sanaga as the longest river entirely in Cameroon, the Logone/Sangha drainage, and the triangle shape. Climate zone names should be checked against the textbook used for the syllabus.
Syllabus references and scope to be checked against the official GCE Board syllabus; all facts, names and figures to be verified by a geography teacher before release.

blocks.md: Cameroon lies in Central Africa on the Gulf of Guinea, between Nigeria to the west and Chad, the Central African Republic, the Congo, Gabon and Equatorial Guinea to the east and south. It is shaped like a triangle with its apex at Lake Chad in the north and its base on the Atlantic coast. It covers about 475 000 km². The capital is Yaoundé and the economic capital is Douala. The country has **ten regions**: Adamawa, Centre, East, Far North, Littoral, North, North West, South, South West and West.

items.text: Far North: Sahelian, Lake Chad basin, Mandara Mountains
Schematic north-south sketch, not a map

blocks.caption: Natural regions from north to south (schematic)
blocks.alt: Four horizontal bands showing the Far North, the North, the highlands and plateau, and the south.

blocks.title: Relief regions
blocks.md:
- **Coastal plain:** low, hot and wet, with mangroves and sandy and muddy shores.
- **Southern plateau:** a forested plateau, about 650 m high, that covers much of the Centre, South and East.
- **Western highlands:** volcanic mountains such as Mount Cameroon, Manengouba, Bamboutos and Oku, with fertile soils and cooler climate.
- **Adamawa plateau:** a high plateau, around 1 000 m, in the centre.
- **Northern lowlands:** the Benue basin and the Chad basin, with the Mandara Mountains in the Far North.

Cameroon is often called **Africa in miniature** because it contains most of Africa's landscapes and climates: equatorial forest, savanna, desert-edge Sahel, mountains and coast. In the south the **equatorial climate** brings heavy rain with two rainy seasons; the coast and Mount Cameroon slopes receive very heavy rain in a long wet season; the **Adamawa and western highlands** are cooler; the north has a **tropical** (Sudanian) climate and the Far North a **Sahelian** climate with a short rainy season.

blocks.title: Rivers and vegetation
blocks.md: Rivers flowing to the Atlantic: the **Sanaga** (the longest river wholly in Cameroon), **Wouri**, **Nyong**, **Ntem** and **Mungo**. Rivers flowing to the interior basins: the **Benue** (towards the Niger), the **Logone** (towards Lake Chad) and the **Sangha** system in the south-east (towards the Congo basin). Vegetation changes from rainforest and mangroves in the south, to savanna with scattered trees in the centre and north, and thorn steppe in the Far North.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Cameroon does not have one single climate; it has several, arranged from south to north.
- Mount Cameroon is in the South West, near Buea and Limbe.
- Do not confuse the Wouri (Douala) with the Sanaga (Edea).
- 'Africa in miniature' is a description of variety, not of size.

blocks.title: Example 1: explain a climate contrast
blocks.statement: Why is the Far North of Cameroon much drier than the South?
steps: The south is close to the equator and the Atlantic, so moist air and convectional rain are frequent.
The Far North is far from the sea and close to the Sahara, with a short rainy season.
Therefore the rainy season is short and rainfall small.
blocks.answer: Because it is far from the sea and near the Sahara, so it has a short rainy season.

blocks.title: Example 2: identify a region from clues
blocks.statement: A region has volcanic soils, mountains above 2 000 m, a cool climate and dense population. Which relief region is it?
steps: Volcanic mountains with cool climate suggest highlands.
Fertile volcanic soil attracts farmers and a dense population.

lessons.title: People and economic activities of Cameroon
lessons.programRef: GCE O Level Geography — Regional geography: Cameroon (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Describe the distribution and main characteristics of the population
Name the main economic activities and the regions where they are important
Explain the problems of development and possible solutions
reviewNotes: Population statement (more than 25 million), SONARA at Limbe, main export items and regional specialisation to be verified against current sources. No statistics are given deliberately.
Syllabus references and scope to be checked against the official GCE Board syllabus; all facts, names and figures to be verified by a geography teacher before release.

blocks.md: The population of Cameroon is young and growing, with more than 25 million people. Most people used to live in the countryside, but the proportion living in towns has risen quickly. Cities such as Douala and Yaoundé are the largest. People belong to many ethnic groups and speak many local languages as well as English and French, the two official languages.

blocks.caption: Main economic activities of Cameroon
blocks.alt: Four boxes: agriculture, forestry, energy and mining, and services with examples.

blocks.title: Main activities
blocks.md:
- **Agriculture:** employs a large share of people: food crops for the home market and cash crops (cocoa, coffee, cotton, banana, rubber, oil palm) for export.
- **Forestry:** timber from the southern and eastern forests.
- **Oil and gas, mining and hydropower:** crude oil is one of the main exports.
- **Industry:** food processing, drinks, timber, cement, aluminium, and others, mainly around Douala.
- **Services:** trade, transport, tourism, banking, telecommunications.

The coast and the Mount Cameroon area receive important investment: ports, plantations, the oil refinery at Limbe and tourism. The Grassfields of the West and North West have dense farming populations. The north produces cotton and cattle. The south supplies cocoa and timber. This regional specialisation makes **internal trade** important and shows why roads and railways matter.

blocks.title: Problems of development
blocks.md: Poor roads and electricity supply; reliance on a few raw exports whose prices change; unemployment, especially among young people; rural-urban migration; pressure on forests and soils; insecurity in some regions; limited processing of raw materials in the country.

blocks.title: Possible solutions
blocks.md: Invest in roads, railways, ports and power; process more raw materials in the country; train workers and support small businesses; protect forests and wildlife; and diversify the economy so that it does not depend on one or two products.

blocks.title: Example 1: diversification
blocks.statement: Why is it risky for a country to depend on one export crop such as cocoa?
steps: If the world price falls, the country's income falls sharply.
Bad weather or disease can destroy the crop.
Diversification spreads the risk across several products and industries.
blocks.answer: Because a fall in price or crop failure would cause a large loss of income.

blocks.title: Example 2: matching activity to region
blocks.statement: Which region is most associated with cotton and cattle: the North or the South West?
steps: Cotton needs a long dry season and cattle need grassland.
These conditions are found in the savanna North.
The South West is wetter and known for plantations and oil refining.

lessons.title: Africa: relief, rivers, climate and resources
lessons.programRef: GCE O Level Geography — Regional geography: Cameroon (to be checked)

objectives: Locate the main physical features of Africa
Describe the pattern of climate and vegetation belts
Name the main mineral and energy resources and the regional groupings in outline
reviewNotes: Facts to verify: 54 states, 'second largest continent', Kilimanjaro as the highest peak, Nile described as among the longest rivers (the ranking is debated), the ordering of bands and the regional groups.
Syllabus references and scope to be checked against the official GCE Board syllabus; all facts, names and figures to be verified by a geography teacher before release.

blocks.md: Africa is the second largest continent after Asia. The equator crosses it near the middle, so it has tropical climates on both sides of the equator. Most of Africa is a high plateau. The **Sahara** is the largest hot desert in the world. Mountain ranges include the **Atlas** in the north-west and the **Drakensberg** in the south; **Kilimanjaro** in Tanzania is the highest mountain on the continent.

items.text: Kalahari and Namib deserts, southern coast
Schematic: climate belts from north to south

blocks.caption: Climate and vegetation belts of Africa (schematic)
blocks.alt: Horizontal bands for Mediterranean, Sahara, savanna, equatorial forest, savanna and southern deserts.

blocks.title: Rivers and lakes
blocks.md:
- The **Nile** is usually counted among the longest rivers in the world and flows north to the Mediterranean.
- The **Congo** carries a huge volume of water through the equatorial region.
- The **Niger** flows through West Africa and the **Benue** is its main tributary.
- The **Zambezi** has the Victoria Falls.
- **Lake Victoria** is the largest lake of Africa; Lake Chad is shared by Cameroon, Chad, Niger and Nigeria.

Climate and vegetation belts are arranged in a roughly **symmetrical** pattern on each side of the equator: equatorial rainforest, then tropical savanna, then desert, then Mediterranean climate near the northern and southern tips. Rainfall decreases with distance from the equator and east-west differences are caused by relief and ocean currents.

blocks.title: Resources and regions
blocks.md: Africa has gold, diamonds, copper, bauxite, iron ore, phosphates, oil and natural gas, along with large hydroelectric potential and fertile land. Major minerals are exported unprocessed, so there is a drive towards local processing. Regional groups include the **African Union** (the continental organisation), **ECOWAS** (West Africa) and **CEMAC** (Central Africa).

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- Africa has 54 recognised sovereign states (check the latest count).
- Do not say that Africa is all desert or all forest; the belts are varied.
- The Sahara is the largest hot desert, not the largest desert in the world, because Antarctica is larger.

blocks.title: Example 1: locate
blocks.statement: Arrange these from north to south: equatorial forest, Sahara, Kalahari, Mediterranean coast (north).
steps: Then the Sahara, then the equatorial forest in the middle.
The Kalahari lies in the south.
blocks.answer: Mediterranean coast, Sahara, equatorial forest, Kalahari.

blocks.title: Example 2: explain the pattern
blocks.statement: Why do the climate belts of Africa repeat on both sides of the equator?
steps: The sun's heat is greatest near the equator and decreases with distance.
The wind and rainfall patterns are similar on both sides.
blocks.answer: Because the sun's heating and wind patterns are similar north and south of the equator.
